probes.name: P5a-tally
probes.subject: tools/tally.py
probes.note: 🔴 AC-5 P5a for `tally`. Print PASS on the failing path while `main` still returns 1 — error #13 exactly: the report says one thing, the gate reads the other, and nothing fails. The `should_pass` assertion above it stays green (the process really did exit 1), so the RED is the disagreement and not a broken fixture.

probes.name: P5a-absent
probes.subject: tools/absent.py
probes.note: P5a for `absent`. AC-5 predicts each instrument's row reddens on its own mutation while the others stay green; running the same defect at each site one at a time is what shows the guard is per-instrument rather than one shared assertion that happens to fire.

probes.name: P5b-tally-exit
probes.subject: tools/tally.py
probes.old: return EXIT_PASS if ok else EXIT_FAIL
probes.note: The other half of #13, and the reason the fixture-forcing assertion exists at all: break the EXIT rather than the printed line. Without this assertion an instrument that always exited 0 and always printed PASS would satisfy 'the two agree' perfectly — the guard would be vacuous in exactly the direction it is meant to catch.

probes.name: P5c-driver-verdict
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_battery.py
probes.note: P5a for the driver, whose token is `PROBE-BATTERY: PASS|FAIL` rather than the shared `VERDICT:` line. A battery that always prints PASS while exiting 1 is the highest-consequence instance of #13 in this repo: the battery report is the evidence every witnessed RED rests on.

exemptions.test_the_verdict_extractors_pass_their_o: Instrument control (Lesson #0056): `_read_verdict_line` is the parser every agreement reading passes through. Breaking it deliberately would redden every probe in this battery at once rather than isolating one claim — a control is asserted green, not probed.
Instrument control, the driver-token half. Same reasoning: it is the reading instrument, not the subject, and P5c is the tool-side mutation that exercises what it reads.
